quizName: DMV Practice Test #10 40 Questions • Passing Score 32

questions.question: What can happen if you shift to a lower gear while going too fast?

options.text: Your motorcycle may jerk and the rear tire may skid.
The horn may sound.
Your motorcycle may jerk and the front tire may skid.
Your motorcycle may jerk and a warning light will turn on.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your motorcycle may jerk and the rear tire may skid.
questions.explanation: If you shift to a lower gear while going too fast, your motorcycle may jerk and the rear tire may skid. This can cause you to lose control. Always slow down before shifting to a lower gear.

questions.question: How can a motorcyclist prevent other drivers from sharing their lane?

options.text: Ride on the left side of the lane.
Ride in the center of the lane.
Give dirty looks to drivers who move into your lane.
Ride in a zigzag pattern to fill up the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center of the lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane to discourage other drivers from trying to squeeze in next to you.

questions.question: When should you check your mirrors?

options.text: Mirror checks are not important.
Only on long trips.
As part of your regular scanning routine.
They don't help since you can't do anything about what is behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: As part of your regular scanning routine.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often as part of your normal routine. Also check mirrors before changing lanes, at intersections, and before slowing down.

questions.question: What should you do when riding at night?

options.text: Be ready to change your lane position as conditions change.
Travel faster than usual to reach your destination quickly.
Always use your low beam headlight to see better.
Stay very close to the vehicle ahead of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to change your lane position as conditions change.
questions.explanation: Be ready to change your lane position, especially at night. Use safe riding strategies when conditions are not ideal.

questions.question: When does alcohol start to impair your riding ability?

options.text: After the first drink.
At about half the legal limit.
At the legal limit.
Only after multiple drinks.

questions.correctAnswerText: After the first drink.
questions.explanation: Even one drink can hurt your riding ability. You can be impaired well below the legal limit. It is never safe to drink and ride.

questions.question: Are intersections safe for motorcycle riders?

options.text: Yes, because there is a lot of traffic there.
No, they are dangerous for riders.
They can be hard to understand.
Yes, they are safer than the open road.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, they are dangerous for riders.
questions.explanation: Intersections are dangerous because many crashes happen there between motorcyclists and other drivers.

questions.question: How should you stop your motorcycle quickly?

options.text: Release the throttle and use the front brake.
Use only the rear brake.
Use only the front brake.
Use both brakes together.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes together.
questions.explanation: To stop quickly, press both brakes at the same time.

questions.question: What lane position should you use when riding?

options.text: Always stay away from the left side of the lane.
Always stay away from the right side of the lane.
Always stay away from the center of the lane.
Use whichever position is safest.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use whichever position is safest.
questions.explanation: There is no single lane position you must always avoid. Change your position based on road conditions.

questions.question: How do headache, cold, and allergy medicines usually affect you?

options.text: They make you sleepy.
They make you more alert.
They make you hungry.
They make it hard to focus.

questions.correctAnswerText: They make you sleepy.
questions.explanation: Most medicines for headaches, colds, allergies, and nerves can make you sleepy and hurt your riding ability. Know how a medicine affects you before you ride.

questions.question: How should you brake to stop quickly?

options.text: Use only the front brake.
Use only the rear brake.
Use the front brake first, then the rear brake.
Use both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: To stop quickly, press both brakes at the same time.

questions.question: When approaching railroad tracks that cross your lane at an angle, what is usually safest?

options.text: Ride straight within your lane to cross the tracks.
It is dangerous to ride straight within your lane to cross the tracks.
It is not safe to cross tracks on a motorcycle.
Ride on the shoulder of the road to cross the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride straight within your lane to cross the tracks.
questions.explanation: When you approach railroad tracks that cross your lane at an angle, ride straight across them while staying in your lane. Turning to cross at a 90-degree angle is dangerous because you could move into another lane of traffic.

questions.question: What often causes a motorcycle to move into another lane while taking a curve?

options.text: Taking the turn too fast.
Lanes that are too narrow.
Not knowing how to steer.
Lanes that are too wide.

questions.correctAnswerText: Taking the turn too fast.
questions.explanation: Entering a curve or turn at too high a speed can cause you to cross into another lane or leave the road.

questions.question: Your lane position should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Help you avoid road hazards.
Help you avoid other drivers' blind spots.
Help you avoid being seen by other drivers.
Make it easier for others to see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help you avoid being seen by other drivers.
questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you see and be seen, keeps you out of other drivers' blind spots, helps you avoid surface hazards, shows your intentions to others, protects you from wind blasts, and gives you an escape route if needed.

questions.question: When should you use the front brake?

options.text: Every time you slow down or stop.
Only when slowing or stopping on slippery roads.
Only when slowing or stopping in an emergency.
Only when slowing or stopping in traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Every time you slow down or stop.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: A proper lane position can help you do all of the following, except:

options.text: Avoid other drivers' blind spots.
Increase your ability to see and be seen.
Go faster.
Set up for turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: Go faster.
questions.explanation: Your lane position helps you see and be seen, avoid other drivers' blind spots, and prepare for turns. It does not help you go faster.

questions.question: What should you do to make a quick stop on wet pavement?

options.text: Use only the front brake.
Use only the rear brake.
Use both brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes to make a quick stop on a slippery surface. The front brake is safe to use on a slippery surface if you apply it gradually to avoid locking the wheel.

questions.question: What is engine braking?

options.text: It is illegal.
It is slowing down by turning the engine off.
It is slowing down by downshifting.
It is not encouraged because it damages the engine.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is slowing down by downshifting.
questions.explanation: Shifting to a lower gear slows you down in a way similar to using the brakes. This is called engine braking.

questions.question: When passing parked cars on your right with no oncoming traffic, where should you stay?

options.text: Stay toward the right side of your lane.
Stay toward the left side of your lane.
Look to your left frequently.
Use your rearview mirrors more frequently than usual.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay toward the left side of your lane.
questions.explanation: When passing parked cars, stay on the side of your lane away from the cars. This protects you from dangers like car doors opening or people stepping out from between the cars.

questions.question: How do you stop in the shortest distance on a straight road?

options.text: Use only the rear brake.
Use only the front brake.
Use both brakes without locking either wheel.
Use both brakes while locking the rear wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes without locking either wheel.
questions.explanation: On a straight road, use both brakes to stop in the shortest distance. Avoid locking either brake.

questions.question: What is true about more than half of all motorcycle crashes?

options.text: They happen at night.
They are caused by bald tires.
They occur at speeds above 55 mph.
They involve inexperienced riders.

questions.correctAnswerText: They involve inexperienced riders.
questions.explanation: More than half of all motorcycle crashes involve riders with less than six months of riding experience. Most crashes happen during the day when riders are going at low speeds.

questions.question: If you need to brake and swerve to avoid a hazard, what should you do?

options.text: Brake first then swerve, or swerve first then brake.
Brake and swerve at the same time.
Choose to either brake or swerve, not both.
Never swerve. Only use the front brake to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake first then swerve, or swerve first then brake.
questions.explanation: Do these actions one after the other, not at the same time. Braking while swerving can cause your motorcycle to tip over.

questions.question: How can you ride more safely at night?

options.text: Night riding is not recommended.
Wear reflective clothing.
Night riding is not safe because other drivers cannot see your turn signals.
Only ride at night in the city.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear reflective clothing.
questions.explanation: Wear reflective materials when riding at night. This makes you more visible to other drivers.

questions.question: How should you check tire pressure?

options.text: Look at the tire. That is good enough.
Use a tire gauge.
Squeeze the tire with your hand.
Compare the tire height to another tire.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use a tire gauge.
questions.explanation: Always use a tire gauge to check pressure before every ride. A tire that looks fine may actually be under-inflated.

questions.question: Where is the rear brake pedal usually located?

options.text: On the left handgrip
On the right handgrip
Near the left footrest
Near the right footrest

questions.correctAnswerText: Near the right footrest
questions.explanation: The rear brake pedal is located near the right footrest on a motorcycle.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT required for an eye or face shield to work well?

options.text: Free of scratches
Resistant to breaking through
Fastens securely
Airtight

questions.correctAnswerText: Airtight
questions.explanation: Good eye protection must be free of scratches, resistant to breaking, fasten securely, and allow air to pass through. It does not need to be airtight.

questions.question: What reduces the effects of alcohol in your body?

options.text: Exercise
Coffee
Time
Food

questions.correctAnswerText: Time
questions.explanation: Your liver breaks down alcohol at a fixed rate. Nothing can speed this up. Only time will reduce alcohol's effects on your body.

questions.question: When you are making a turn, what happens if you need to stop?

options.text: You have less traction available for stopping.
You have more traction available for stopping.
Stopping is the same as on a straight road.
You should never try to stop while turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: You have less traction available for stopping.
questions.explanation: When leaning to turn, some traction is used for turning. This leaves less traction for braking. Braking while turning is possible but requires extra care.

questions.question: When following another vehicle as a new rider, what should you do?

options.text: Keep at least four seconds of distance between you and the other vehicle.
Get as close as possible to the other vehicle.
Do not worry about how far back you are.
Always ride on the left side of the lane so the driver can see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep at least four seconds of distance between you and the other vehicle.
questions.explanation: Beginning riders should keep at least four seconds of distance behind the vehicle ahead. Increase this distance if road or weather conditions are poor.

questions.question: When borrowing a motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Skip the tire pressure check.
Assume it handles like your own motorcycle.
The owner will check the brakes, so you do not have to.
Give yourself extra space and time to react.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give yourself extra space and time to react.
questions.explanation: Do all the same safety checks on a borrowed motorcycle as you would on your own. Ride carefully and give yourself extra room to stop.

questions.question: How should a motorcycle be fitted to you?

options.text: Your feet should touch the ground when you are seated.
The seat should be even with your waist.
The seat should be 10 inches above your waist.
The seat should be 10 inches below your waist.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your feet should touch the ground when you are seated.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle fits you properly when your feet can touch the ground while seated. When riding, keep your feet firmly on the footrests.

questions.question: If a dog chases your motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Swerve around the dog.
Stop and wait for the dog to lose interest.
Ride alongside the dog.
Slow down, then speed up quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, then speed up quickly.
questions.explanation: If a dog chases you, slow down as you approach it. Then speed up and leave it behind.

questions.question: A leather jacket:

options.text: Makes a rider look cool.
Is usually too warm to wear while riding.
Protects you if you crash.
Should never be worn while riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Protects you if you crash.
questions.explanation: Wear a long-sleeved leather jacket when riding for protection. Modern motorcycle jackets protect you while keeping you cool in hot weather.

questions.question: The front brake provides how much of a motorcycle's stopping power?

options.text: About one-quarter
About one-half
About three-quarters
All of it

questions.correctAnswerText: About three-quarters
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It provides about three-quarters of the motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: Why should motorcycle riders not rely only on mirrors to see around them?

options.text: Motorcycle mirrors are smaller, so you can't see as much.
Motorcycles have blind spots, just like cars.
Mirrors are never accurate.
Mirrors take your eyes off the road and should not be used.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorcycles have blind spots, just like cars.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like any other vehicle. You cannot rely only on mirrors to know what is behind you. Turn your head to check your blind spots regularly.

questions.question: Your space cushion while riding should:

options.text: Always stay the same.
Change based on riding conditions.
Not be necessary in most situations.
Be avoided to keep traffic moving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change based on riding conditions.
questions.explanation: Increase your space cushion when your motorcycle needs more distance to stop, when roads are slippery, when you cannot see ahead clearly, or when traffic is heavy.

questions.question: A rectangular sign shows:

options.text: School crossing
Railroad crossing
Stop
Speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs like speed limits are rectangular with white background and black letters or symbols. Follow the rules on these signs.

questions.question: Your lane position should:

options.text: Keep other drivers from sharing your lane.
Give you a good view of the scenery.
Place you in other drivers' blind spots.
Hide your plans from other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep other drivers from sharing your lane.
questions.explanation: A good lane position keeps you out of blind spots, helps you see and be seen, avoids surface hazards, protects you from wind blasts, and gives you an escape route. Position yourself so other drivers won't try to share your lane.

questions.question: To swerve, you should:

options.text: Turn the handlebars quickly.
Shift your weight quickly.
Press the handgrip toward the direction you want to go.
Press the handgrip away from the direction you want to go.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handgrip toward the direction you want to go.
questions.explanation: To swerve, press the handgrip on the side where you want to turn. To swerve left, press the left handgrip then the right to recover. To swerve right, press the right handgrip then the left.

questions.question: In group riding, this hand signal means:

options.text: Speed up.
Danger ahead.
Stop.
Merge.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop.
questions.explanation: When the lead rider extends their left arm straight down with palm facing back, the group should stop.

questions.question: Where is the engine cut-off switch located?

options.text: Near the left handgrip
Near the right handgrip
Near the left footrest
Near the right footrest

questions.correctAnswerText: Near the right handgrip
questions.explanation: The engine cut-off switch is next to the right handgrip. Know where all your motorcycle's controls are before you ride.
